title: Clo Vendor Leaderboard - Strategic Vision
description:
We’re officially debuting the CLO Vendor Leaderboard, a platform created to connect brands with the most innovative 3D-ready partners in the industry. This year, we’re spotlighting pioneers across Hong Kong and Southeast Asia: Busana Apparel Group, Cobalt Fashion, Crystal International, GMS+, Hop Lun, Newtimes Group, Daehan Global, PT. Kahatex, and Trax Intertrade.

In the fifth CLO Vendor Leaderboard video series, Stategic Vision, we look beyond today's workflows to explore the Strategic Vision of the world's leading apparel manufacturers. As we wrap up our multi-part series on digital transformation in the garment industry, we asked our global manufacturing partners a critical question: What is your long-term strategic vision for 3D adoption? The answers prove that the industry is hitting a massive tipping point. 3D is shifting from a design "backup plan" into an integrated data backbone.

This series covers the 5 essentials of 3D success: 
1️⃣ 3D Capacity 
2️⃣ Investment & Resources 
3️⃣ Business Impact 
4️⃣ Partnership
5️⃣ Strategic Vision 

⏱️ Timestamps 
00:15 – Making Digital-First the Absolute Default
05:04 – The AI Revolution: Hyper-Realism & Automation
07:02 – What does the apparel supply chain look like 10 years from now?

✨ Thank you for tuning into our series! Revisit our previous episodes on communication, onboarding, and scaling 3D tech on our channel.

markdown_content: ## Integration of CLO3D with AI for Enhanced Design and Visualization This section discusses the strategic advantage of combining CLO3D software with artificial intelligence (AI) tools to improve garment design, visualization, and customer engagement. Key terms include CLO3D, AI integration, hyper-realistic visualization, and digital garment animation. Combining CLO3D with AI tools offers significant benefits in both the design process and garment visualization. The integration enables hyper-realistic animations where customers can see models wearing garments with fabric movement, increasing engagement. This combination is seen as the future of design, retail, and marketing, providing an advancement beyond traditional visualization tools. The company’s long-term vision includes integrating 3D technology throughout all stages of design, sampling, and production—not only as a visualization aid but also as a decision-making tool. To prepare, internal workflows are being standardized, and the team remains actively engaged with software updates and beta features. The goal is to operate seamlessly between digital and physical production pipelines, facilitating faster, more efficient product development. New and existing customers receive bespoke presentations introducing them to 3D services, where some of their existing styles are converted into 3D. This includes demonstrations of style and fabric manipulations, helping clients understand the value of 3D in their development processes. With the industry trending toward shorter lead times and faster turnarounds, 3D adoption is positioned as a critical enabler to meet these demands. --- ## Vision for Digital-First Product Development and Production Efficiency This section outlines the company’s vision of making digital-first the default approach in product development and production, emphasizing 3D’s role in cost control, efficiency, and sustainability. Important topics include digital product lifecycle, SMV (Standard Minute Value), fabric usage optimization, and waste reduction. The long-term goal is to reduce physical samples to one or two per product, using 3D as the integrated backbone of the development process instead of a standalone tool. Digital product creation will immediately provide key metrics such as Standard Minute Value (SMV) and fabric usage, updated in real time as designs evolve. Systems will also help reduce cutting waste and identify opportunities to produce additional products from leftover materials. This integrated approach benefits multiple functions: - Merchandisers receive early visibility of assortments. - Production teams gain better data for capacity planning and efficiency. - Marketing obtains rich digital assets for storytelling and sell-in, eliminating the wait for physical samples. Expanding 3D capacity strengthens sustainability by reducing waste and accelerating decision-making. This strategy builds industry-wide trust by demonstrating a commitment to faster, better, and more sustainable production. --- ## Embedding 3D as a Scalable Organizational Capability This section describes how 3D technology is being embedded as a scalable system across the organization, not just a skill of individual users. It covers digital asset management, workflow standardization, cross-stream training, and integration with product lifecycle management (PLM) software. The company is developing robust digital assets and standardized workflows to make 3D an essential, scalable part of the organization. Cross-stream training ensures that 3D is not limited to a single person’s skill set but is broadly adopted across teams. Preparation for future CLO advancements includes staying close to new features such as fabric simulation, scan automation, AI-driven pattern generation (patent-to-3D), and tighter integration with PLM systems. The objective is to connect 3D directly with real business outcomes such as fewer physical samples, faster decision-making, greater customization, and cleaner data flows. Strengthening internal connectivity between CLO and CloSet platforms aims to streamline file sharing between departments—from design to pre-production—enhancing visibility, decision clarity, and operational efficiency. --- ## Leveraging 3D Prototypes in Physical Showrooms for Cost and Risk Reduction This section explains the use of 3D prototypes in physical showroom environments to visualize product variations and reduce physical setup costs, time, and risks. By expanding 3D prototypes in showrooms, teams can preview various product choices, locations, and variations virtually before investing in physical setups. This reduces overall costs and minimizes risks associated with physical sample production and display, accelerating decision-making and product iteration. --- ## Sustainability Through Virtual Sampling and Digital-First Design Workflows This section focuses on how 3D technology supports sustainability by reducing material waste, shipping emissions, and sample production. Key concepts include virtual sampling, carbon footprint reduction, digital asset libraries, and sustainability metrics. Virtual sampling enabled by 3D reduces fabric waste and decreases the need for shipping physical samples. The company actively encourages clients to adopt a digital-first design process, where the first sample is approved virtually before any physical prototype is produced. This approach supports environmental goals and allows smarter, data-driven production planning. Benefits include: - Ordering less sample fabric. - Producing fewer samples at proto, sales, and fit stages. - Building reusable digital asset libraries for future collections. These measures contribute to long-term cost savings and efficiency improvements while reducing the carbon footprint. Sustainability is quantified by tracking the number of sample rounds avoided as a measurable matrix tied directly to 3D adoption. For example, one client implemented a digital-first photo policy requiring 3D approval before physical samples, resulting in a 50% reduction in fabric waste and sample shipments within a single season. This client now fully embraces 3D as their default development approach, demonstrating the scalability and impact of digital-first strategies. --- ## Future Outlook: AI Integration and End-to-End 3D Product Lifecycle This section explores the anticipated integration of AI with CLO3D and the evolution of 3D technology in the complete product lifecycle, from design to sales. Future developments are expected to include AI-powered avatars and virtual try-ons that are photorealistic and simulate realistic movements for various scenarios such as sports, activewear, workwear, and uniforms. AI may also enable retroactive pattern creation from garment images, fitting patterns directly to avatars. These advancements will accelerate speed and accuracy in rendering, reducing errors and waste during manufacturing. CLO3D and 3D technology will become fully integrated into the end-to-end product lifecycle, extending beyond sampling to support demand testing, digital assortment planning, and pre-production reselling. This evolution aims to improve the overall experience for brands and consumers, shaping the future of the fashion and apparel industry through faster, more sustainable, and more precise digital workflows.
